title: Vinícius Jr.'s Brilliance Rescues Brazil From Morocco in a Group C Classic
excerpt: Ismael Saibari's composed chip gave Morocco the lead before Vinícius equalised with a trademark solo strike at MetLife Stadium
body:
## The Headline Match Delivers

The scheduling gods had been kind: the only first-round meeting between two top-10 FIFA-ranked sides, played on a sun-drenched Saturday afternoon in northern New Jersey. No. 6 Brazil versus No. 7 Morocco — five-time champions against 2022 semi-finalists, Seleção swagger against Atlas Lions ferocity. The 80,663 fans at MetLife Stadium got exactly the spectacle they came for.

## Morocco Draw First Blood

For the opening 20 minutes, Morocco were the better side by a distance. Walid Regragui's team pressed Brazil high, won physical duels, and looked like the team with the pedigree. In the 21st minute, Brahim Díaz found Ismael Saibari with a perfectly weighted through-ball that split Marquinhos and Gabriel Magalhães. Saibari, demonstrating composure that belied the occasion, chipped the ball over the onrushing Alisson and into the net for his 10th international goal.

It was a statement of intent from the reigning AFCON champions. Morocco led in expected goals (1.28-0.86), total shots (12-6), and duels won (61-51) in the first half. The physicality that had carried them to a historic 2022 semi-final was on full display, and Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil looked sluggish, frustrated, and a step behind.

## The Vinícius Moment

Eleven minutes later, the best player on the pitch decided to remind the world why he had won the 2024 FIFA Best Men's Player award.

Vinícius Jr. exchanged a quick combination with Bruno Guimarães on the left flank, took two touches to create a yard of space, and unleashed a right-footed shot that flew past the outstretched arm of Yassine Bounou. It was clinical, it was beautiful, and it was his 10th goal in 50 national team appearances. The yellow-clad Seleção fans, who had gone uncharacteristically quiet after Saibari's opener, erupted.

## Ancelotti's Halftime Surgery

At the break, Ancelotti made decisive changes: Fabinho replaced the poor Casemiro, and Danilo came on for Roger Ibáñez. The substitutions steadied Brazil's ship without fundamentally altering the balance of the game. The second half was a more cautious affair — Morocco controlled possession while Brazil sat deeper, content to counterattack.

Lucas Paquetá, who Sporting News would later describe as having a "disasterclass," was mercifully withdrawn for Luiz Henrique on the hour. Matheus Cunha's introduction gave Brazil more dynamism, and Raphinha tested Bounou with a low drive, but neither side could find a winner.

In the final minutes, both teams had chances: Alisson produced a superb double save to deny Nayef Aguerd and the follow-up, while Danilo forced Bounou into a sharp stop from inside the box. The final whistle confirmed what both managers probably knew at halftime: 1-1 was a fair result.

## The Desi View from East Rutherford

MetLife Stadium sits in the heart of the NJ/NY tri-state area — home to one of the densest concentrations of South Asian Americans in the country. Indian-American fans made their presence felt in the stands, many sporting Brazil jerseys alongside Indo-Caribbean supporters who had come to cheer both teams. For the desi community of Jersey City, Edison, and Iselin, the World Cup was not across an ocean for once — it was a 20-minute drive up the Turnpike.

## Group C After Matchday 1

Scotland's 1-0 win over Haiti in the late game means Group C has an early leader, with Brazil and Morocco level on one point each. Brazil next face Haiti on Friday in Philadelphia — a match they will be expected to win comfortably. Morocco take on Scotland in Foxborough the same day. Neither the Seleção nor the Atlas Lions will be losing sleep over this result; at a 48-team World Cup, a draw in the toughest group game is a perfectly acceptable start.

But Brazil will know they were second-best for long stretches. Without Neymar — still recovering from a torn right calf — and with Casemiro and Paquetá both struggling, Ancelotti has selection headaches to address before Friday.
